newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Water to form holding company.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Water to form holding company.

text.p: California Water Service Co said Wednesday its board of directors voted to form a holding company.

"The water industry is becoming more competitive. Investor-owned utilities are competing against each other as well as against entities that are not regulated by the California Public Utilities Commission, including special water districts and large contract-service providers," said Robert Foy, chairman of Cal Water.
Under Cal Water's current organization as an investor-owned, regulated California utility, the CPUC has jurisdiction over the company's unregulated operations.
A holding company structure will allow financing flexibility and eliminate uncertainty concerning the allocation of costs between regulated and unregulated business operations.
Shareholders are expected to vote on the plan in April 1997. Initially, the holding company is expected to have one wholly owned subsidiary, California Water Service Co.
The name of the holding company has not yet been chosen.
California Water Service is the largest investor-owned water utility in California and the third largest in the U.S.
